details:
GEOVISTA Intelligence Platform is a multi-source geospatial AI system for Earth Observation modeling, hazard forecasting, and decision support. It ingests data from 11 satellite and reference providers, including MODIS, Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-1 SAR, NISAR, and ESA WorldCover. Six specialist deep learning model families then cover vegetation, land cover, change detection, flood inundation, coastal dynamics, and ground deformation. A FastAPI backend serves training and inference asynchronously, and a React and OpenLayers dashboard lets users explore maps, time series, and forecasts.

https://bramha-geovista-t6rj.vercel.app/

We also designed a dedicated SAR image-processing chip, a hardware accelerator that speeds up synthetic aperture radar processing. It is written in Verilog and verified through simulation in Vivado, and it points toward faster, low-power onboard or edge processing of radar imagery.

Benefits and impact: The platform brings fragmented optical and radar data into one place, so planners and researchers can anticipate floods, coastal erosion, and ground deformation earlier. Our flagship PyTorch VegetationLSTM, trained on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 GPU, reached a validation R² of 0.9384.

Tools: Python, PyTorch, FastAPI, React, OpenLayers, Node.js, Vercel, Verilog, and Vivado.

Creativity: We fuse optical and SAR sources, which see through clouds and darkness, and combine specialist models through ensemble weighting. What sets the project apart is the custom SAR image-processing chip, which extends the work from software into hardware. Instead of relying only on general-purpose GPUs, we explore dedicated silicon for radar processing, closing the loop from chip to model to dashboard.

Factors considered: Data diversity, accuracy, scalability, accessible visualization, hardware efficiency, and running on modest consumer hardware.
